M1.title: Authenticated tailnet chat stream proof
M1.outcome: From Expo Go on the phone, over the tailnet only, a user can send one prompt to the currently resident Ollama model and watch the reply stream in token by token, protected by a bearer token, with Stop working.

review_override.reason: Human authorised a third fix cycle beyond the 2-cycle cap (cycle 5) to fix the cycle-5 review's IMPORTANT finding: FR13 401 handling must show 'password wrong or changed' and route to Settings.

as_built.result: RECORDED — 62/62 files attributed; components C1,C2,C3,C4,C6,C7,C8,C9,C10,C11; 12 edges; 2 claim mismatches (C5 claimed but not in diff, deferred to M2 per code comments; C3 present but not claimed)

criteria.text: With a model already resident in Ollama, sending a prompt from the Expo Go app over Tailscale Serve renders the reply incrementally, token by token, ending in a terminal complete state.
evidence: e2e-tailnet-proof.sh (live, tailnet URL :8443): 80 content events over ~6.5s ending done status complete — .harness/evidence/M1-T5b-verifier.log
server.test.ts chat streams content then complete — .harness/evidence/M1-T7-verifier.log
On-phone Expo Go rendering: human check, not yet done

HUMAN CHECK 2026-09-25 (after cycle-2 review, finding B): on the iPhone with Tailscale ON, Expo Go opened exp://ryans-mac-studio.tailc3648a.ts.net:8081, hung on 'Opening project', then showed 'Unmatched Route'. The app did not reach the chat or Settings screens; token paste, streaming and Stop could not be tried. FAIL.

CYCLE-2 FIX (M1-C6, commit 1a7565e): cause of 'Unmatched Route' was that mobile/src/app had no index.tsx, so the root path Expo Go opens matched no screen. Added index.tsx redirecting to /setup (no token) or /chat (token); bundle host restarted; the tailnet-served bundle registers ./index.tsx. The ~20s 'Opening project' wait matches the first production bundle build (bundle-host.log: 'iOS Bundled 23140ms'). On-phone re-test by the human: pending.

HUMAN CHECK 2026-09-25 (re-test after fix cycle 2): on the iPhone with Tailscale ON, Expo Go opened the app and reached the Setup screen (Unmatched Route is fixed). On Setup, the on-screen keyboard covers the submit (Continue) button and does not dismiss when tapping outside the input; the human could not get past Setup. Chat, Settings, streaming and Stop could not be tried. FAIL.

CYCLE-3 FIX (M1-C9 81d49c6, M1-C10 61421a3): Setup, Settings and Chat now move their content above the keyboard (KeyboardAvoidingView; Setup/Settings offset by the header height), tapping or dragging outside the input dismisses it, and the token field is single-line with a Done key that submits. Chat's duplicate top bar removed. Bundle host restarted; tailnet-served bundle carries the change. On-phone re-test by the human: pending.

HUMAN CHECK 2026-09-25 15:51 (re-test after fix cycle 3; screenshots in ~/.claude/uploads/a2032993-e031-4e36-92d7-4ddfdde26a07/): Setup PASSED - the token was pasted and Continue reached Chat. Chat: the human sent 'Test' and received the reply 'Hello! How can I assist you today?' (the end-to-end send and reply work on the phone). FAIL: on Chat, the keyboard covers the message input box. Chat still shows two top bars (a Stack header 'chat' above the screen's own 'Chat / Settings' bar), although M1-C9 claimed to hide the Stack header. Settings opens (Stack header '< chat' / 'settings', with Cancel, Save and Logout); keyboard behaviour on Settings was not reported. Token-by-token rendering and Stop not yet reported.

HUMAN CHECK 2026-09-25 15:53 (after a full force-close and reopen of Expo Go; screenshot ~/.claude/uploads/a2032993-e031-4e36-92d7-4ddfdde26a07/1eae7b80-image.png): the app now fails at launch with the Expo Go error screen: 'There was a problem running "Phone Models". Unhandled JS Exception: TypeError: Cannot convert Symbol to string', stack: anonymous (expo-router.bundle ... :60047:56) < RootLayout (:58345:55) < WrappedScreenComponent (:76671:49) < Suspense < ZoomTransitionTargetContextProvider. This suggests the 15:51 run was a cached pre-cycle-3 bundle (two top bars on Chat), and the current cycle-3 bundle crashes in RootLayout. FAIL.

CYCLE-4 FIX (M1-C11 6fec6a1, M1-C12 49bb53f, M1-C13 0376cf3): launch crash on every launch with a stored token fixed (Fragment inside RootLayout's <Stack>; present since d87a597); Chat/Settings now always get their declared options, so after first-time Setup Chat has one top bar and its keyboard offset premise (no Stack header) holds. New runtime check `cd mobile && bun run smoke:runtime` executes the production iOS bundle in Node with fake native modules: proves launch + first screen render without a JS exception for token present (Chat) and absent (Setup), and the Setup -> Chat path with one top bar; cannot prove Hermes-only behaviour, native layout/keyboard geometry, or anything past first screens. Bundle host restarted; served bundle passes the runtime check. On-phone re-test by the human: pending.

HUMAN CHECK 2026-09-25 (re-test after fix cycle 4, iPhone with Tailscale ON, all eight recorded cycle-4 steps): the human reported 'All working'. AC1 steps: fresh force-close/reopen landed on Chat with no error; one top bar; message box and Send stayed above the keyboard; a short prompt streamed word by word and finished; second force-close/reopen landed directly on Chat. PASS.
Final review cycle 6 (sonnet, 650e350): PASS; independent re-run in .harness/evidence/M1-cycle6-review.log

criteria.text: The server and the app bundle are reachable from the phone over the tailnet and are not reachable from a device on the LAN or the public internet.
evidence: e2e: 7789 listens on 127.0.0.1 only; tailnet :8443 200; LAN 192.168.0.27 refuses 7789 and 8443; 8081 manifest via tailnet name 200 — .harness/evidence/M1-T5b-verifier.log
GAP: LAN 8081 (Expo bundle host, binds *:8081) is currently REACHABLE; closing it needs a human-run sudo pf command; LAN-device check is a human check

HUMAN CHECK 2026-09-25: after the human ran `sudo bash ops/scripts/install-pf-anchor.sh` (LaunchDaemon com.harness.pf-bundle-host installed, loader last exit 0), the human opened http://192.168.0.27:8081 in Safari on the iPhone with Tailscale OFF on the home Wi-Fi: it FAILED TO LOAD. Note: e2e-tailnet-proof.sh run on the Mac itself still reports LAN 192.168.0.27:8081 REACHABLE (HTTP 200) after install; the Mac-local probe may not exercise the LAN path (unconfirmed).

CYCLE-2 FIX (M1-C7, commit 1a248cf): the Mac-local LAN 8081 probe (routes over lo0, always REACHABLE) was replaced by checks that the pf LaunchDaemon's last exit is 0 and its loaded interface equals the current tailnet utun; live e2e exit 0 — .harness/evidence/M1-C7-verifier-2.log. The human LAN-device check above remains the LAN evidence.

M2b.title: Swap-load and unload from the phone, staying resident
M2b.outcome: From the phone a user can load a model (a swap: every other resident model is unloaded first) or unload the resident one; the operation runs asynchronously while the app polls GET /v1/state through loading to ready or a specific failure reason, and a model loaded from the phone stays resident indefinitely (keep_alive -1), including across chat replies. The confirmation rule for a reply in flight or a resident model not loaded by this server belongs to M2c.

criteria.text: Loading model A then model B leaves only B resident in GET /api/ps; unloading leaves nothing resident.
A model loaded from the phone remains resident in GET /api/ps after 10 minutes idle and after a chat reply completes.
A failed load, such as out of memory, leaves nothing resident and the app shows the failure reason.

complexity_check_at_pickup.decision: run without a further split: M2b is itself the child of the M2 split made at pickup for exactly this signal pair; every one of its three criteria is a live observation of the same load/unload lifecycle (requirements: all ACs proven against the live Mac), so no criterion-conserving seam separates implementation from live proof, and moving M2-AC3 out would leave the pair intact in the remainder. Estimated 3 worker tasks, ~6 production files, 2 subsystems (server, mobile). Recorded for human visibility under Follow-ups.

M2c.title: Busy confirmation before a swap or unload
M2c.outcome: Before a swap or unload, the server answers 409 confirmation_required with its reasons when a reply is in flight or the resident model was not loaded by this server; the app shows that warning (the other-tool case labelled as a best approximation), confirming cancels any in-flight reply and proceeds, and cancelling the confirmation leaves state unchanged.

criteria.text: Swapping or unloading while a reply is in flight, or while the resident model was not loaded by this server, requires explicit confirmation, and cancelling the confirmation leaves state unchanged.

M3.title: Persisted multi-turn conversations with model attribution
M3.outcome: The phone keeps a list of conversations, each with full multi-turn history sent on every prompt, each reply labeled with the model that produced it, and conversations survive an app restart.

criteria.text: Conversations can be created, opened and deleted, and are listed newest first.
A follow-up prompt in the same conversation demonstrably uses context from an earlier turn.
Each assistant reply displays the model name that produced it, including after a mid-conversation model switch.
Sending with no model resident is blocked with a prompt to load one.
Force-quitting and reopening Expo Go shows the same conversations and messages as before.

M4.title: Thinking display and dropped-connection resume
M4.outcome: Reasoning output appears collapsed and expandable, separate from the answer, and a transport drop or app backgrounding mid-reply resumes cleanly with no gaps or duplication once the phone reconnects.

criteria.text: For a model that emits reasoning output, the app shows it in a collapsed, expandable section separate from the answer.
Killing the connection mid-reply and reconnecting yields the complete reply with no gaps and no duplicated text.
Backgrounding the app mid-reply and returning to foreground resumes the same reply and receives its terminal state, with only an explicit Stop cancelling generation.

M5.title: Always-on Mac tooling, plain-language errors, and PWA retirement
M5.outcome: The server and app bundle host survive a Mac reboot with no manual step, every failure mode shows a distinct plain-language message, and the old PWA is retired without disturbing the harness's own endpoint.

criteria.text: After a Mac reboot, opening the project in Expo Go on the phone works with no manual step on the Mac.
Killing either the server process or the bundle host process causes it to restart automatically.
The app shows a distinct message for each of: Mac or server unreachable, Ollama down, wrong password, model failed to load, model no longer installed, and reply already in progress.
After retirement, /app no longer resolves, the PWA's LaunchAgent is gone, and the harness's / handler still works.
